title: OTEL middleware exception when ran via Streamlit's Starlette but not Uvicorn direct
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Open Telemetry (OTEL) has a [Starlette instrumentation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib/tree/main/instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-starlette). Streamlit wraps Starlette via [`st.App`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/server/st.app) (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7667, https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600). Therefore, I expect to be able to OTEL monitor Streamlit (at least API if not also UI). Instead, `streamlit run` fails to start with `AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'add_middleware'` where same code works for running via `uvicorn`.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from opentelemetry import metrics
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.starlette import StarletteInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import PeriodicExportingMetricReader, ConsoleMetricExporter
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from starlette import applications
from starlette.middleware import Middleware
from starlette.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.routing import Route
from streamlit.starlette import App
import streamlit as st


st.markdown("Home")

async def api_health(request):
    return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy"})

### DIFF
## - (A) 🚩 FATAL: AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'add_middleware'
app = App(
## - (B) 👌 works but only Starlette API-responsive not Streamlit UI
# app = applications.Starlette(
### 
    "home.py",
    routes=[Route("/api/health", api_health) ],
    middleware=[Middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=['127.0.0.1', 'localhost'])]
)

StarletteInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
resource = Resource.create(attributes={"service.name": "starlette-service"})
reader = PeriodicExportingMetricReader(ConsoleMetricExporter())
meterProvider = MeterProvider(resource=resource, metric_readers=[reader])
metrics.set_meter_provider(meterProvider)

### RUN
## - (A) python -m streamlit run home.py
##      🚩 FATAL: AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'add_middleware'
## - (B) python -m uvicorn home:app 
##      http://localhost:8000/api/health succeeds 
##      after 60s get OTEL metrics logged to console
###
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install
    ```bash
    $ python --version
    Python 3.14.7
    $ pip install streamlit opentelemetry-sdk opentelemetry-instrumentation-starlette
    $ streamlit --version
    Streamlit, version 1.62.0
    ```
2. Toggle+run example code path `(A)` to see Streamlit error vs `(B)` to see working Starlette/Uvicorn.

### Expected Behavior

I expect Streamlit's `app` to expose Starlette's `add_middleware` functionality, especially where `middleware` was explicitly defined.



### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Mac M4 27.0
- Browser: Firefox 156.0


### Additional Information

Use Case: I assume like all of us, I'm just trying to get to working metrics data. The rabbit hole I found myself in is it appears perhaps metrics like this emitted historically under `--global.metrics=true` but which is now deprecated. So originally started at [this Discuss](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/performance-monitoring-ideas/5205) which sublinks to FR https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/373 and https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16730 which led to [this Discuss](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/prometheus-integration-for-streamlit-app-metrics/61731) which suggested OTEL (along a custom `streamlit_extras` build-out) so I tried it with default setup and its Starlette works Uvicorn-layer but not Streamlit-layer where I want/need. TIA!

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16997)

`st.App` is an ASGI wrapper around Starlette (composition, not a subclass), so OpenTelemetry's `StarletteInstrumentor.instrument_app()` fails with `AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'add_middleware'`. Middleware is accepted only at construction (`App(..., middleware=[...])`) and applied later when the inner Starlette app is built lazily on the first ASGI call; there is no `add_middleware` (or `router` / `user_middleware`) surface for post-construction instrumentors. The working uvicorn path in the report uses vanilla `starlette.applications.Starlette`, not `st.App` — `uvicorn home:app` with `st.App` would hit the same error at import time. A likely fix is to add a Starlette-compatible `add_middleware` that appends to `_user_middleware` before the inner app is built; full OTEL compatibility may also need other Starlette attributes that instrumentors inspect. Passing OTEL's ASGI middleware via the constructor is a possible workaround today.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9159 — Open request for first-class OpenTelemetry / observability support; this report is a compatibility gap while trying to use existing Starlette OTEL instrumentation with `st.App`.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11126 — DataDog auto-instrumentation request; same class of third-party ASGI/Starlette instrumentors expecting a real Starlette (or similarly introspectable) app.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600 — Starlette/ASGI `st.App` introduction (closed RFF). Documents custom middleware as a supported `App` feature, but only via the constructor, which is what OTEL's `instrument_app()` does not use.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

>  Passing OTEL's ASGI middleware via the constructor is a possible workaround today.

Can you try passing the middleware via the constructor? From looking at the code [here](https://github.com/huyan0/opentelemetry-python/blob/34698ff82dd0003c78893fbf78e3ec6e9022b68a/ext/opentelemetry-instrumentation-starlette/src/opentelemetry/instrumentation/starlette/__init__.py#L24), it might work like this: 

```python
from opentelemetry.ext.asgi import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.starlette import _get_route_details

app = st.App(
    "home.py",
    routes=[Route("/api/health", api_health) ],
    middleware=[
           Middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=['127.0.0.1', 'localhost']),
           Middleware(OpenTelemetryMiddleware, span_details_callback=_get_route_details)
    ]
)
```

Thanks [USER] , 

AFAICT `add_midldeware` is Starlette/FastAPI ad not OTEL related ([example](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/middleware/#adding-asgi-middlewares)), so it should instead be a Streamlit-to-Starlette implementation that this sub-function doesn't surface/exist. 

Or if your code snippet (thanks!) worked on your machine, it reports same error on mine:

```python
from opentelemetry import metrics
# from opentelemetry.ext.asgi import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.asgi import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.starlette import _get_route_details
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.starlette import StarletteInstrumentor
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import PeriodicExportingMetricReader, ConsoleMetricExporter
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from starlette import applications
from starlette.middleware import Middleware
from starlette.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.routing import Route
from streamlit.starlette import App
import streamlit as st

st.markdown("Home")

async def api_health(request):
    return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy"})

app = App(
    "home.py",
    routes=[Route("/api/health", api_health) ],
    middleware=[
         Middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=['127.0.0.1', 'localhost'])
        ,Middleware(OpenTelemetryMiddleware, span_details_callback=_get_route_details)
    ]
)

StarletteInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
resource = Resource.create(attributes={"service.name": "starlette-service"})
reader = PeriodicExportingMetricReader(ConsoleMetricExporter())
meterProvider = MeterProvider(resource=resource, metric_readers=[reader])
metrics.set_meter_provider(meterProvider)

# python -m streamlit run home.py
# # 🚩 FATAL: AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'add_middleware'
# # same stack trace
```

Nitpicks: ported to [official code](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-contrib/blob/main/instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-starlette/src/opentelemetry/instrumentation/starlette/__init__.py#L213), from [pip](https://pypi.org/project/opentelemetry-instrumentation-asgi/) switched import to `from opentelemetry.instrumentation.asgi import OpenTelemetryMiddleware`.

Cheers!
The Middleware is meant to be used as replacement for `StarletteInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)`, calling instrument_app will always raise this error with the current Streamlit version.

🙏 Thank you for your feedback! 

Closing as resolved with final minimal working example (of domain not sub-routes):

```python
from opentelemetry import metrics
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.asgi import OpenTelemetryMiddleware
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics import MeterProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.metrics.export import PeriodicExportingMetricReader, ConsoleMetricExporter
from opentelemetry.sdk.resources import Resource
from starlette.middleware import Middleware
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.routing import Route
from streamlit.starlette import App
import streamlit as st

st.markdown("Home")

async def api_health(request):
    return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy"})

app = App(
    "home.py",
    routes=[Route("/api/health", api_health) ],
    middleware=[Middleware(OpenTelemetryMiddleware)
    ]
)

resource = Resource.create(attributes={"service.name": "starlette-service"})
reader = PeriodicExportingMetricReader(ConsoleMetricExporter(), export_interval_millis=5000)
meterProvider = MeterProvider(resource=resource, metric_readers=[reader])
metrics.set_meter_provider(meterProvider)

# python -m streamlit run home.py
```
